chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning one who claimed the slave of a man and asserted that he was his son, that he is to be freed from the wealth of the one who claimed him. If the claimant dies and his wealth is divided before the slave is freed, then the wealth has preceded him; but if he is freed before his wealth is divided, then he has his share from it.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, whose judicial ruling is being transmitted
key_terms.عَبْدَ إِنْسَانٍ: the slave belonging to a person
key_terms.مِنْ مَالِ الَّذِي ادَّعَاهُ: from the estate of the one who made the claim
key_terms.يُعْتَقُ: is to be emancipated or set free

ai.seo_question: If a man acknowledges a slave as his son, does the slave become free and inherit from him?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام about a person who acknowledges a slave as his son. The slave is to be emancipated from the claimant’s estate, and his right to inherit depends on whether emancipation occurs before or after the estate is divided.
